chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) led his companions in prayer on the day they were martyred, then he said: 'I testify that permission has been granted for your killing, O people! So fear Allah and be patient.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husayn say to his companions before their martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual composure of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as he led the final prayer before his martyrdom, affirming the divine decree of their sacrifice. By stating that permission for their death had been granted, he transformed their impending defeat into a conscious act of worship, urging his companions to maintain *taqwa* and *sabr* in the face of inevitable fate. This moment underscores the Shia theological view that the Battle of Karbala was not merely a historical tragedy but a pre-ordained cosmic event fulfilling divine will.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me (from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh), from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, from Naďr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā ibn ‘Imrān Al-Ḥalabi, from Ḥusain ibn Abil ‘Alā, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Ḥusain (a.s.) led the (Fajr) prayer for his companions on the day on which they were assaulted and then said, “O people! I testify that permission has been granted for you to be killed, so fear Allāh and remain patient.”
